committed: Before any implementation output was inspected: this file and the validation contract in TIDAL_KERNEL.md were committed ahead of js/kernels/tides/, the validation tool, the oracle's script and results, and the tests. No number below is the output of the kernel; every closed-form value is a relation between a function's arguments and its result, and every published value was typed from the cited source and not re-read (checked: false).

model.name: equilibrium tides with a frequency-independent quality factor (constant Q)
model.units: SI throughout: m, kg, s, W, J
model.torque: N = (3/2) (k2/Q) G m^2 R^5 / a^6 on a body of radius R raised by a perturber of mass m at a circular orbit of radius a (Goldreich and Soter 1966), signed by sgn(spin - n)
model.recession: da/dt = 3 (k2/Q) (m/M) (R/a)^5 n a, with n = sqrt(G (M + m) / a^3); equivalently da/dt = C a^(-11/2) with C = 3 (k2/Q) (m/M) R^5 sqrt(G (M + m)); closed form a(t)^(13/2) = a0^(13/2) + (13/2) s C t
model.spin: I domega/dt = -dL/dt with L = mu sqrt(G (M + m) a), mu = M m / (M + m), I = alpha M R^2 (alpha 0.3307 for the Earth); the sum L + I omega is conserved exactly by construction
model.heating: Edot = (21/2) (k2/Q) G M^2 n R^5 e^2 / a^6 for a synchronously rotating satellite of radius R on an orbit of semi-major axis a and small eccentricity e about a primary of mass M (Peale, Cassen and Reynolds 1979); a leading-order-in-e formula
model.locking: t_lock = I omega / N with N the torque above and I = alpha m_s R^2: the time for a constant torque to remove the spin omega; the printed forms of the despinning time differ by a factor 2 through the definition of Q, so this one is derived from N and stated, not quoted
model.bulge: equilibrium tide, peak to trough: (3/2) h2 (m/M) (R/d)^3 R from the quadrupole potential G m r^2 P2(cos psi) / d^3 divided by the surface gravity G M / R^2; h2 = 1 for a fluid with no self-gravity correction
model.roche: the existing authority js/tidalPhysics.js: rigid 2^(1/3) R (rho_p / rho_s)^(1/3); fluid coefficient 2.44 (Roche 1850, the value in most texts); the exact incompressible synchronous value 2.4553 (Chandrasekhar 1969) is a named option
model.resonance: a ring particle inside a moon of semi-major axis a_m is in the p:q mean-motion resonance (p > q >= 1 integers, T_m / T_r = p / q) at a_r = a_m (q / p)^(2/3); a point-mass Kepler relation with no oblateness
model.toomre: Q_T = c kappa sigma_v / (3.36 G Sigma) for a particle disc and pi in place of 3.36 for a fluid disc; kappa = Omega for a Kepler disc

a1.roche.closed.what: rigid limit from densities equals 2^(1/3) R_p (rho_p / rho_s)^(1/3), equals the mass form 2^(1/3) R_s (M_p / m_s)^(1/3), and tidal-to-self-gravity at that distance is 1; equal densities give 1.25992 R_p; the fluid-to-rigid ratio is 2.44 / 2^(1/3); a satellite denser than its primary is flagged inside the primary

a2.bulge.closed.what: the equilibrium peak-to-trough height equals (3/2) h2 (m/M) (R/d)^3 R against the oracle; scales as d^-3, as m, and as h2 exactly; P2 factors 1 and -1/2 reproduce 3/2 of the peak

a3.heating.closed.what: Edot against the oracle for six parameter sets; exactly proportional to e^2 and to k2/Q; scales as a^(-15/2) at fixed primary (n a^-6); energy per orbit equals Edot times the period; Edot is zero at e = 0

a4.evolution.closed.what: da/dt, the torque, domega/dt against the oracle for six parameter sets; the closed form a(t) against scipy's DOP853 integration of da/dt at rtol 1e-12; timeToReach is the inverse of a(t); L + I omega conserved over 1e9 years; the total energy -G M m / (2 a) + I omega^2 / 2 decreases monotonically (dissipation > 0) while omega > n; the recession sign follows sgn(omega - n)

a5.locking.closed.what: t_lock against the oracle for four parameter sets; proportional to omega, to Q / k2, to a^6 and to 1 / m^2 exactly

a6.rings.closed.what: resonance radius a_m (q/p)^(2/3) against the oracle for 2:1, 3:2, 4:3, 5:3, 7:6; the Kepler period ratio at the returned radius equals p/q; Toomre Q against the oracle for both coefficients

b1.roche.published.what: the coefficients against their sources: 2^(1/3) = 1.26 (Murray and Dermott 1999) within 0.1 percent, the fluid default 2.44 equal to Roche's value, the option 2.4553 equal to Chandrasekhar's within 0.01 percent; and the published findings Phobos orbits (9,376 km from the centre of Mars; Mars radius 3,389.5 km, density 3,933 kg/m^3; Phobos density 1,876 kg/m^3) outside the rigid and inside the fluid Roche limit; Shoemaker-Levy 9's perijove (1.3 Jupiter radii; Jupiter density 1,326 kg/m^3; nucleus density 600 kg/m^3, Asphaug and Benz 1994) inside the fluid limit; the Moon (density 3,344 kg/m^3) at 384,400 km outside the fluid limit of the Earth

b2.moon.recession.what: the Moon's recession with k2 = 0.30 and Q = 12 for the Earth (equatorial radius 6.3781e6 m, mass 5.9722e24 kg, spin 7.2921159e-5 rad/s, alpha 0.3307), the Moon at 3.844e8 m (7.342e22 kg): da/dt against the lunar laser ranging value 3.82 +/- 0.07 cm per year (Dickey et al. 1994), within 10 percent; the length of day's tidal lengthening against 2.3 ms per century (Stephenson and Morrison 1995), within 15 percent

b3.io.heating.what: Io (radius 1.8216e6 m, a 4.217e8 m, e 0.0041, Jupiter 1.8982e27 kg) with k2 = 3/2 and Q = 100: the prediction lies within a factor 2 of the observed total heat flow range 6e13 to 1.6e14 W (Veeder et al. 1994; Spencer et al. 2000), and an order-of-magnitude bound is returned: the maximum heating for k2 = 3/2 and the smallest Q the model accepts is above the observed range; the k2/Q the observed mid-range requires is below 3/2 / 5

b4.cassini.gap.what: Mimas (semi-major axis 1.8552e8 m, the value js/tidalPhysics.js holds) at the 2:1 resonance puts a ring particle at 1.1687e8 m; the observed outer edge of the B ring, the inner edge of the Cassini Division, is 117,580 km (Porco et al. 2005): the point-mass resonance radius lies within 1.0 percent of it. The bound is the size of the neglected oblateness correction, J2 (R_S / r)^2 about 0.004 to 0.006, chosen before the kernel was run; it is not tuned to a result

b5.locking.published.what: the Moon (k2 0.024, Q 100, alpha 0.393, radius 1.7374e6 m, mass 7.342e22 kg, about the Earth at 3.844e8 m) and Io (k2 1.5, Q 100, alpha 0.38, radius 1.8216e6 m, mass 8.932e22 kg, about Jupiter at 4.217e8 m) are observed to be tidally locked: for an initial spin of one rotation per 10 hours the kernel's locking time is below 4.5e9 years for both (Phobos and the other locked moons are not tested for want of a quotable k2; the Earth is not tested as a negative case because its spin has not been slowed to locking and the model's time is of the order of the age)

c.ensemble.what: not applicable and stated: the kernel returns closed-form values with no uncertainty estimator, so no stated uncertainty can be covered; the published tier (b) carries the comparison with measurement

d.refusals.what: every hostile or out-of-domain input is refused with its named code and never returns a number: non-finite, zero and negative masses, radii, distances and densities; Q below 5 or above 1e7; k2 at or below 0 or above 3/2; heating eccentricity below 0 or above 0.1; an orbit at or inside the primary; a resonance with p <= q or non-integer order; evolution that crosses corotation (spin equal to the orbital rate) inside the interval, which names the time; strings, objects, undefined
